How to navigate

Choose a focus, then Render room. Changes apply on Render; this is a still capture, not live orbit. For close-ups, choose the matching scene setup first.

Experimental sampling and optical transport. Not real-time or quality-qualified. Captures retain source provenance, actual sample counts and linear HDR.

Advanced settings · sampling, materials and placement
Sampling and presentation
The primary fixed-camera path separates lighting and path choices across pixels and events. Camera points remain stable, including the centre at one SPP. Image quality and cost require scene qualification.

Splitting requires the stable sampler and adds secondary rays, not camera SPP. Material inspection requires guided denoising; its first-sample colour and normal guides are diagnostic, not photographic output. Uniform sampling removes the radial budget bands.

Lighting and surface materials

External daylight is supplied because the room has no authored lights. Cool evening is a colour study, not a solar-position simulation. Varnish requires layered clearcoat; it adds a coating to verified seat wood without rewriting source assets. These switches remain independent.

Glass and water experiment
Requires nested refraction and volume metadata. Uses authored roughness/transmission; not alpha holes or subsurface scattering.
Requires bounded nested transport and no splitting. Ordinary scattering keeps its own limit; every optical event still costs work and bounded storage.
Zero preserves contact. A positive value lowers only the pedestal, leaving the glass and camera fixed. This floating test isolates coincident surfaces; it is not a realism correction.

Glass-to-water image quality and performance are not yet fully qualified. The glass preset enables bounded branching and nested refraction. Rough optical transport stays off unless selected explicitly. Legacy splitting can overflow and reject a capture. Water overlaps the thick glass slightly, without a fake air gap; a neutral pedestal supports it. Six bounces may terminate longer paths. Off restores the original room.

Models and placement

Original chair and ottoman inside the server-selected room (verified on Render). No added studio walls or ceiling panel. Placement moves the Eames pair; the camera target stays fixed. Centre reference exchanges sofa and spacesuit positions only. The sofa is uniformly scaled to 1.5 m wide, preserving its proportions; the standing model keeps its source scale. Wall collisions are not checked.

Additional assets are loaded only from the local server and verified on Render.

Laboratory diagnostics · separate tests, not scene presets

The white-light diagnostic compares normal maps on/off and pixel-centre/multi-sample camera rays, using the selected camera, SPP ceiling and sheen. No shadows, indirect bounces, splitting or denoising. Not a full render or performance benchmark.

Splitting comparison uses room framing, radial default-ceiling budgets and the stable sampler; denoising, glass, varnish and close-up settings do not apply. One warmup, three rotated timing rounds, then diagnostic images. Keep the tab visible; this may take several minutes.

Scene qualification captures empty glass, filled glass and the room at 1080p and 4K, uniform 32 SPP and 20 bounces. Runs sequentially, stops on failure and retains HDR, counts and provenance. This can take considerable time; it does not certify image convergence or performance. Cancel stops the sequence.

Recorded for reproducible independent-noise controls. Does not change the scene.

Convergence prequalification resets scene controls to the original filled room, then captures uniform 32/128/256 SPP with seeds 7 and 19 at native 1080p and 4K. This is a long-running correctness job, not a performance test. Each completed lane is retained; Stop prevents further lanes. Offline HDR analysis is required before any convergence claim.
